defects: Faint vertical light streaks/banding columns under the ensō and type in the later frames (visible in pairs rows 2–3), which look like a compositing or texture-tiling artifact
The ensō write-on reads as a constant-speed trim path that sweeps around the circle with no pressure ramp, so the brush has no weight or hesitation where it lands or lifts
'Brush' pops in whole between samples (absent at the red-stroke frame, then fully there), with no build and no relationship to the strokes
The last ~1.5 s is static: per-second change drops to 1.7, and the only motion is the bottom squiggle drawing on
The brush texture is a flat vector fill with procedural dry-brush slits. It has no ink density variation, wet edge, bleed or paper interaction
The bold geometric sans 'Brush' clashes with the calligraphic strokes and has no typographic tie to the brush idea
The layout is a specimen sheet (circle left, stack of samples right) rather than a composition. Frames 1–3 are mostly empty and the final frames are cluttered with four unrelated marks
gaps: Motion: everything is a sequential linear write-on (circle, then red, then type, then line, then squiggle) with no overlap, easing, brush-speed variation or follow-through. Top studio work would vary stroke speed with pressure, overlap the reveals and choreograph a handoff between marks

Structure/idea: there is no arc and no payoff. It builds marks into a static brush-preset sheet, with dead air at the end and no ending that rhymes with the opening stroke, camera move or transformation

Finish: the vector brush has no material quality (ink pooling, paper grain, light falloff), the type pops in flat, and there are visible vertical streak artifacts. At award level the ink should feel physically wet and the frame should hold up as a poster
